cards.definition: **Definition.** A transformed test-specific value that can be compared with a family-level alpha to implement a named multiplicity procedure under its assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting an adjusted p-value as a posterior false-discovery probability for that individual hypothesis.
cards.prompt: What does adjusted p-value diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A transformed test-specific value that can be compared with a family-level alpha to implement a named multiplicity procedure under its assumptions.

cards.definition: For a least-squares model with an intercept, n observations, and design rank p including the intercept, assume n>p and TSS>0. Adjusted R² is 1-[RSS/(n-p)]/[TSS/(n-1)]. It penalizes residual reduction by lost residual degrees of freedom, can be negative, and need not rise when a predictor is added. It does not itself estimate future predictive performance.
major_error_concepts: Adjusted R² is always between zero and one and always increases when a predictor is added.
cards.prompt: State adjusted R² for an intercept least-squares model, declaring how parameters and degrees of freedom are counted.
required_concepts: State 1-[RSS/(n-p)]/[TSS/(n-1)] with p including the intercept.
Require positive residual degrees of freedom and TSS.
The value can decrease or be negative.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Regression analysis of an assigned-condition contrast with pre-treatment covariates included to improve precision or account for design features under a predeclared functional form.
major_error_concepts: Adjusting for post-treatment variables or selecting covariates from outcome significance while claiming an ordinary randomized contrast.
cards.prompt: Define ANCOVA adjustment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: ANCOVA analyzes an assigned-condition contrast using regression with pre-treatment covariates.
Covariate adjustment is predeclared to improve precision or account for design features under a stated functional form.

accepted_variants: Reject each valid p_i≤alpha/m. The union bound gives FWER≤alpha even with dependent tests, and FDR≤FWER, so it also controls FDR.
cards.definition: For m prespecified hypotheses with valid marginal p-values, Bonferroni rejects H_i when p_i≤alpha/m, equivalently when min(1,m p_i)≤alpha. It controls familywise error at alpha under arbitrary dependence. Consequently it also bounds the false discovery rate by alpha, although FWER is its primary and stronger error target.
major_error_concepts: Bonferroni divides observed p-values by m and does not control the probability of any false rejection.
cards.prompt: State Bonferroni correction, its dependence assumptions, and the relation between its FWER and FDR guarantees.
required_concepts: Use alpha/m per test or adjusted p-values min(1,m p_i).
The principal guarantee is FWER≤alpha without requiring independence.
FWER control also implies FDR control; this true consequence is not a major error.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A coefficient, contrast, or prediction interval formed from a declared regression bootstrap scheme and replicate statistic distribution.
major_error_concepts: Reporting bootstrap quantiles without identifying the resampling unit, refitted pipeline, target statistic, or interval method.
cards.prompt: Define bootstrap regression interval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A coefficient, contrast, or prediction interval formed from a declared regression bootstrap scheme and replicate statistic distribution.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Resampling observational rows or independent sampling units with replacement and refitting the entire regression pipeline on each pseudo-sample.
major_error_concepts: Resampling dependent rows independently or keeping data-selected preprocessing fixed while claiming full-pipeline bootstrap uncertainty.
cards.prompt: Define case bootstrap for regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Resampling observational rows or independent sampling units with replacement and refitting the entire regression pipeline on each pseudo-sample.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A mapping from category levels to design-matrix columns with an explicit reference or constraint that determines coefficient interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting indicator coefficients without identifying the reference level and included interactions.
cards.prompt: Define categorical predictor encoding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A mapping from category levels to design-matrix columns with an explicit reference or constraint that determines coefficient interpretation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A sandwich-based coefficient standard error allowing arbitrary error dependence within declared clusters while relying on suitable across-cluster conditions and cluster counts.
major_error_concepts: Treating cluster-robust inference as valid with any number of clusters or as protection against dependence across clusters.
cards.prompt: Define cluster-robust standard error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A cluster-robust standard error uses a sandwich estimator that allows arbitrary error dependence within declared clusters.
Its validity still relies on suitable across-cluster conditions and an adequate number of clusters.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The level within which observations may have dependent errors and across which clusters are treated as independent for a cluster-robust procedure.
major_error_concepts: Choosing the clustering column solely because it gives larger or smaller standard errors rather than from the sampling and dependence structure.
cards.prompt: Define clustering unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The level within which observations may have dependent errors and across which clusters are treated as independent for a cluster-robust procedure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interval for a specified regression coefficient formed from its estimate, standard error, reference distribution, and model assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a coefficient interval without stating the design coding or conditioning on other included columns.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient confidence interval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interval for a specified regression coefficient formed from its estimate, standard error, reference distribution, and model assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The property that the model and design determine a unique value for the coefficient or contrast targeted by inference.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every printed coefficient has a unique population interpretation despite rank deficiency or aliasing.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient identifiability. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The property that the model and design determine a unique value for the coefficient or contrast targeted by inference.

cards.definition: For an in-sample least-squares fit with an intercept and TSS=sum_i(y_i-ybar)²>0, R²=1-RSS/TSS, where RSS=sum_i(y_i-yhat_i)². Orthogonal least-squares fitting gives 0≤R²≤1 in this setting. If TSS=0, the usual centered ratio is undefined; the bound need not hold for a no-intercept or out-of-sample calculation.
major_error_concepts: When all outcomes are identical, 1-RSS/TSS always defines R² without a special convention.
cards.prompt: Define the usual centered R² for an intercept least-squares fit, including its denominator and scope.
required_concepts: Define RSS and positive centered TSS in R²=1-RSS/TSS.
The usual in-sample bounds use an intercept least-squares fit.
Constant outcomes with TSS=0 require a separately declared convention.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A fitted or assumed coefficient vector containing many exact zeros relative to its dimension.
major_error_concepts: Equating small coefficients with exact sparsity or interpreting selected variables as a uniquely true subset.
cards.prompt: Define coefficient sparsity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A fitted or assumed coefficient vector containing many exact zeros relative to its dimension.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The estimated repeated-sampling standard deviation of a fitted coefficient under the model and variance assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Treating the coefficient standard error as the standard deviation of the predictor or response.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient standard error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The estimated repeated-sampling standard deviation of a fitted coefficient under the model and variance assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A coefficient estimate minus its null value divided by its estimated standard error, compared with an appropriate reference distribution.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by the coefficient estimate or residual standard deviation instead of the coefficient standard error.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient t statistic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A coefficient estimate minus its null value divided by its estimated standard error, compared with an appropriate reference distribution.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered vector of coefficients aligned one-to-one with the columns of the design matrix.
major_error_concepts: Treating coefficients as an unordered set independent of design-column identity.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient vector. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordered vector of coefficients aligned one-to-one with the columns of the design matrix.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The expected response value given specified predictor values, written E[Y|X=x], and targeted by many regression models.
major_error_concepts: Equating the conditional mean with every individual response at the same predictor value.
cards.prompt: Define conditional mean. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The expected response value given specified predictor values, written E[Y|X=x], and targeted by many regression models.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Confirmatory analysis tests predeclared primary questions under a fixed error plan, while exploratory analysis searches patterns that require transparent labeling and later confirmation.
major_error_concepts: Reconstructing a confirmatory story after exploring many models, outcomes, and subgroups.
cards.prompt: Distinguish confirmatory versus exploratory analysis.
required_concepts: Confirmatory analysis addresses primary questions declared before inspecting the results.
Confirmatory analysis operates under a fixed error-control plan.
Exploratory analysis searches the observed data for patterns or candidate questions.
Exploratory findings require transparent labeling and later independent confirmation before receiving a confirmatory interpretation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Estimation, standard error, interval, or test for c^T beta using the fitted coefficient covariance and a predeclared contrast vector.
major_error_concepts: Adding coefficient standard errors directly while ignoring covariance between coefficient estimates.
cards.prompt: Define linear contrast inference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Estimation, standard error, interval, or test for c^T beta using the fitted coefficient covariance and a predeclared contrast vector.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A deletion-influence measure combining residual size and leverage to summarize how much the fitted regression changes when an observation is removed.
major_error_concepts: Applying a rule-of-thumb cutoff as an automatic deletion command rather than an investigation signal.
cards.prompt: What does Cook's distance diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A deletion-influence measure combining residual size and leverage to summarize how much the fitted regression changes when an observation is removed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Selecting penalty hyperparameters using performance estimated on folds not used to fit each candidate, under a frozen split and metric protocol.
major_error_concepts: Preprocessing on all data before folds or reporting the same cross-validation score as untouched final performance.
cards.prompt: Define cross-validated penalty selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Selecting penalty hyperparameters using performance estimated on folds not used to fit each candidate, under a frozen split and metric protocol.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The matrix whose rows correspond to observations and columns encode intercepts, predictors, transformations, indicators, and interactions used by the linear predictor.
major_error_concepts: Treating the raw data table as the design matrix without accounting for coding, transforms, or column order.
cards.prompt: Define design matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Each row of the design matrix corresponds to one observation used by the model.
Each column encodes a model term such as an intercept, predictor, transformation, indicator, or interaction.
The ordered columns of the design matrix supply the variables used by the linear predictor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Failure of design columns to be linearly independent, making at least some coefficient parameterizations non-unique.
major_error_concepts: Treating rank deficiency as merely high but finite coefficient uncertainty rather than non-identifiability of the chosen parameterization.
cards.prompt: Define design-matrix rank deficiency. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Failure of design columns to be linearly independent, making at least some coefficient parameterizations non-unique.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Penalized regression combining L1 and L2 penalties to balance sparsity and grouped or stabilized shrinkage behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling elastic net equivalent to either ridge or lasso for every mixing value and dataset.
cards.prompt: Define elastic net regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Penalized regression combining L1 and L2 penalties to balance sparsity and grouped or stabilized shrinkage behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A predeclared linear or model-based comparison between assigned conditions aligned with the experiment's target population, outcome, and coding.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a contrast after seeing group means or interpreting a coefficient with the wrong reference and interaction conditions.
cards.prompt: Define experiment treatment contrast. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A predeclared linear or model-based comparison between assigned conditions aligned with the experiment's target population, outcome, and coding.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A conditional response family expressible in exponential-family form, supplying a mean-variance relationship used by a standard GLM.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all exponential-family responses have constant variance or continuous support.
cards.prompt: Define exponential-family response model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A conditional response family expressible in exponential-family form, supplying a mean-variance relationship used by a standard GLM.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A known linear-predictor term with coefficient fixed at one, often log exposure in a count-rate model.
major_error_concepts: Estimating the offset coefficient freely or treating exposure as an ordinary response-independent constant when it varies by unit.
cards.prompt: Define exposure offset. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A known linear-predictor term with coefficient fixed at one, often log exposure in a count-rate model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The probability of making at least one false rejection within a defined testing family under the joint data-generating configuration.
major_error_concepts: Defining FWER as the average per-test Type I error or as the false discovery rate.
cards.prompt: Define family-wise error rate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The probability of making at least one false rejection within a defined testing family under the joint data-generating configuration.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The model's estimated conditional mean for an observation's design row, commonly yhat_i = x_i^T betahat.
major_error_concepts: Calling a fitted mean the observed response or a future realized prediction with no residual uncertainty.
cards.prompt: Define fitted value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The model's estimated conditional mean for an observation's design row, commonly yhat_i = x_i^T betahat.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A model class combining a response distribution from an exponential-family form, a linear predictor, and a link relating that predictor to the conditional response mean.
major_error_concepts: Defining a GLM as any nonlinear regression or omitting the response-family and link contract.
cards.prompt: Define generalized linear model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A generalized linear model specifies a response distribution in an exponential-family form.
It specifies a linear predictor built from the design matrix and coefficients.
It specifies a link function relating the conditional response mean to that linear predictor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The coefficient-linear quantity eta = X beta formed from the design matrix before applying the inverse link.
major_error_concepts: Requiring the linear predictor itself to lie on the response-mean scale.
cards.prompt: Define GLM linear predictor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The coefficient-linear quantity eta = X beta formed from the design matrix before applying the inverse link.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified conditional distribution family for the response given predictors, such as binomial or Poisson, including its variance relationship.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a GLM family solely from the visual shape of fitted values while ignoring response support and conditional variance.
cards.prompt: Define GLM random component. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified conditional distribution family for the response given predictors, such as binomial or Poisson, including its variance relationship.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The linear projection operator H mapping observed responses to OLS fitted values, yhat = Hy, for a fixed full-rank column space or generalized-inverse formulation.
major_error_concepts: Treating the hat matrix as a covariance matrix or assuming its entries depend only on response values.
cards.prompt: Define hat matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The hat matrix H is the linear projection operator associated with the fitted OLS column space.
It maps the observed response vector y to fitted values by yhat=Hy.
The stated operator uses a fixed full-rank column space or the corresponding generalized-inverse formulation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A coefficient standard error derived from a heteroscedasticity-consistent sandwich covariance estimate, relaxing constant conditional variance while retaining other requirements.
major_error_concepts: Claiming robust standard errors repair nonlinear conditional means, dependence, omitted variables, or biased samples.
cards.prompt: Define heteroscedasticity-robust standard error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The standard error is derived from a heteroscedasticity-consistent sandwich covariance estimate.
It relaxes the constant conditional-variance assumption used by the conventional OLS covariance formula.
It does not remove the model's other requirements, such as a suitable conditional mean and dependence structure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A step-down Bonferroni family-wise procedure that orders p-values and compares them with sequential alpha/(m-k+1) thresholds while preserving FWER control under broad dependence.
major_error_concepts: Applying Holm thresholds to unsorted p-values or continuing rejections after the first step-down failure.
cards.prompt: Define Holm multiple-testing procedure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Holm's step-down procedure orders the family of p-values.
It compares the ordered values with sequential alpha/(m-k+1) thresholds and controls FWER under broad dependence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The assumption that conditional error variance is constant across predictor values or fitted means under the model.
major_error_concepts: Calling errors homoscedastic because their overall variance is finite while conditional variance changes systematically.
cards.prompt: Define homoscedastic regression errors. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The assumption that conditional error variance is constant across predictor values or fitted means under the model.

cards.definition: Independent regression errors means that, conditional on the declared design or covariates, the joint error law factors into its component error laws. Independence is stronger than zero pairwise correlation. When errors are clustered or serially dependent, appropriate covariance modeling or robust inference can account for that dependence, but the errors are still not independent.
major_error_concepts: Clustered errors become independent as soon as a cluster-robust standard error is used.
cards.prompt: Define independent regression errors. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The joint conditional error law factors under independence.
Modeling dependence is an alternative assumption, not independence.
Uncorrelated errors need not be independent.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A predicted response for one future observational unit at specified predictor values, combining conditional-mean prediction with irreducible outcome variation.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a fitted conditional mean has no additional uncertainty for an individual future outcome.
cards.prompt: Define individual prediction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A predicted response for one future observational unit at specified predictor values, combining conditional-mean prediction with irreducible outcome variation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An observation whose inclusion materially changes fitted coefficients, predictions, or conclusions under a declared influence measure.
major_error_concepts: Equating every outlying response with influence or deleting influential valid data solely to improve fit.
cards.prompt: What does influential observation diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: An observation whose inclusion materially changes fitted coefficients, predictions, or conclusions under a declared influence measure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A design column whose coefficient allows one predictor's conditional association with the response to vary across another predictor.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting main effects as unconditional averages when an interaction changes their reference-condition meaning.
cards.prompt: Define regression interaction term. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A design column whose coefficient allows one predictor's conditional association with the response to vary across another predictor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Penalized regression using an L1 absolute-coefficient penalty that can set fitted coefficients exactly to zero under the chosen parameterization.
major_error_concepts: Treating a zero lasso coefficient as proof the predictor has no population association or causal relevance.
cards.prompt: Define lasso regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Penalized regression using an L1 absolute-coefficient penalty that can set fitted coefficients exactly to zero under the chosen parameterization.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The diagonal hat-matrix value h_ii measuring how unusual an observation's design row is and how strongly its response can affect its own fitted value.
major_error_concepts: Defining leverage from response extremeness or residual size alone.
cards.prompt: What does regression leverage diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: The diagonal hat-matrix value h_ii measuring how unusual an observation's design row is and how strongly its response can affect its own fitted value.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The joint model probability or density of the observed data viewed as a function of unknown parameters, under a declared sampling structure.
major_error_concepts: Treating likelihood as a normalized posterior probability distribution over parameters without a prior and normalization.
cards.prompt: Define Regression-model likelihood. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The joint model probability or density of the observed data viewed as a function of unknown parameters, under a declared sampling structure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** For nested likelihood-based regression or generalized-linear models, the statistic twice the full-minus-restricted maximized log likelihood is a deviance difference, commonly calibrated by a chi-square law only under the relevant regularity and interior-parameter conditions.
major_error_concepts: Using the ordinary chi-square calibration for nonnested models, unidentified parameters, boundary nulls, or data-dependent model selection without a justified alternative law.
cards.prompt: Define Nested regression likelihood-ratio test.
required_concepts: The test compares nested likelihood-based regression or generalized-linear models.
Its statistic is twice the full-model maximized log likelihood minus the restricted-model maximized log likelihood, equivalently a deviance difference.
The statistic is commonly calibrated against a chi-square distribution.
Chi-square calibration requires the relevant regularity conditions and an interior null parameter rather than a boundary or unidentified case.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified linear combination c^T beta used to express a comparison or model quantity on the coefficient scale.
major_error_concepts: Choosing contrast weights after seeing which combination gives the most favorable result without disclosing selection.
cards.prompt: Define linear contrast of coefficients. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A specified linear combination c^T beta used to express a comparison or model quantity on the coefficient scale.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The assumption that the chosen design columns combine linearly in coefficients to represent E[Y|X] over the analysis domain.
major_error_concepts: Checking only whether each raw predictor has a straight marginal scatterplot and declaring the multiple-regression mean correctly specified.
cards.prompt: Define linearity of the conditional mean. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The assumption that the chosen design columns combine linearly in coefficients to represent E[Y|X] over the analysis domain.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A function g that maps the conditional mean to the linear predictor, g(E[Y|X]) = X beta.
major_error_concepts: Confusing the link with the inverse link or applying it to realized responses as a generic preprocessing transform.
cards.prompt: Define GLM link function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A function g that maps the conditional mean to the linear predictor, g(E[Y|X]) = X beta.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The link g(mu)=log(mu) mapping a positive conditional mean to a real-valued linear predictor.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a log-link coefficient as an additive change on the original response-mean scale.
cards.prompt: Define log link. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The link g(mu)=log(mu) mapping a positive conditional mean to a real-valued linear predictor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The multiplicative change in conditional odds associated with a one-unit coefficient contrast, obtained by exponentiating the corresponding log-odds coefficient.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting an odds ratio as a risk ratio or probability difference without conversion and baseline context.
cards.prompt: How is a logistic regression odds ratio obtained from a coefficient, and how should it be interpreted?
required_concepts: Exponentiating the corresponding log-odds coefficient gives the logistic regression odds ratio.
The odds ratio is the multiplicative change in conditional odds associated with the stated one-unit coefficient contrast.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inverse-logit of a fitted linear predictor, yielding an estimated conditional success probability.
major_error_concepts: Reporting the linear predictor or odds as though it were already a probability.
cards.prompt: Define logistic predicted probability. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inverse-logit of a fitted linear predictor, yielding an estimated conditional success probability.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A binomial GLM using the logit link to model conditional success probability through a linear predictor.
major_error_concepts: Calling logistic regression a model of class labels with normally distributed constant-variance errors.
cards.prompt: Define logistic regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A binomial GLM using the logit link to model conditional success probability through a linear predictor.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The function log(p/(1-p)) mapping a probability p in (0,1) to log odds on the real line.
major_error_concepts: Defining the logit as log probability or as the inverse-logit probability itself.
cards.prompt: Define logit link. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The function log(p/(1-p)) mapping a probability p in (0,1) to log odds on the real line.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Parameter estimation by choosing values that maximize the observed-data likelihood or log-likelihood within the specified model.
major_error_concepts: Claiming the maximum-likelihood estimate is the most probable parameter value in a frequentist model by definition.
cards.prompt: Define maximum likelihood estimation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Parameter estimation by choosing values that maximize the observed-data likelihood or log-likelihood within the specified model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interval for the conditional mean at a specified predictor vector, reflecting coefficient-estimation uncertainty.
major_error_concepts: Calling a mean-response interval a prediction interval for one future observation.
cards.prompt: Define mean-response confidence interval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interval for the conditional mean at a specified predictor vector, reflecting coefficient-estimation uncertainty.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The fitted estimate of E[Y|X=x0] for a specified predictor vector x0.
major_error_concepts: Equating an estimated conditional mean with an individual future outcome.
cards.prompt: Define estimated mean response. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The fitted estimate of E[Y|X=x0] for a specified predictor vector x0.

cards.definition: Deviance measures fitted-model discrepancy from a saturated reference on the same response data. In the usual GLM dispersion convention with common fixed phi>0, scaled deviance is D_s=2[ell_sat(phi)-ell_fit(phi)], and unscaled deviance is D=phi D_s. For an unweighted Gaussian model, D=RSS and D_s=RSS/sigma². Conventions should be named consistently. Nested differences support likelihood-ratio comparisons with compatible likelihood/dispersion handling; an exact chi-square law does not follow automatically.
major_error_concepts: Deviance is twice fitted-minus-saturated log likelihood and is exactly chi-square for every GLM sample.
cards.prompt: What does model deviance diagnose, and how is its saturated-model likelihood discrepancy oriented and scaled?
required_concepts: Deviance measures discrepancy from a saturated fit on the same data.
Orient the likelihood difference as saturated minus fitted and distinguish scaled from unscaled deviance using a consistent dispersion convention.
If nested comparisons are discussed, require compatible likelihood, dispersion, and calibration conditions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A predeclared comparison of target estimates and uncertainty across plausible model terms, variance estimators, exclusions, and coding choices.
major_error_concepts: Searching specifications until one is significant and reporting only that result as robustness.
cards.prompt: What does model-specification sensitivity analysis diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A predeclared comparison of target estimates and uncertainty across plausible model terms, variance estimators, exclusions, and coding choices.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Strong linear dependence among design columns that inflates uncertainty and makes individual coefficient interpretation unstable, without necessarily harming fitted means equally.
major_error_concepts: Claiming multicollinearity biases OLS coefficients automatically or diagnosing it from outcome correlation.
cards.prompt: Define multicollinearity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Multicollinearity is strong linear dependence among design columns that inflates coefficient uncertainty.
It destabilizes individual coefficient interpretation without necessarily degrading fitted means to the same degree.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of hypotheses whose joint error behavior is controlled together, defined by the scientific decision and analysis plan rather than only by one output table.
major_error_concepts: Defining each favorable test as its own family after seeing results to avoid multiplicity correction.
cards.prompt: Define multiple-testing family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A multiple-testing family is the set of hypotheses whose joint error behavior is controlled together.
The scientific decision and prespecified analysis plan determine which hypotheses belong to the family.
A single software output table does not by itself define the scientific testing family.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A multiple-testing problem evaluates a declared family of hypotheses jointly because the chance and expected proportion of false rejections depend on the entire decision family, not only each marginal test level.
major_error_concepts: Claiming that testing every member of the family at per-test level alpha automatically controls the family-wise error rate at alpha.
cards.prompt: Define multiple testing problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A multiple-testing problem evaluates a declared family of hypotheses jointly.
False-rejection probability and expected false-rejection proportion depend on the full decision family, not only on each marginal test level.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A comparison in which the reduced model is obtained by constraining parameters of the full model, using the same response observations and compatible likelihood or loss.
major_error_concepts: Calling models nested because one has fewer terms even when they use different responses, transformations, observations, or incompatible families.
cards.prompt: Define nested model comparison. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The reduced model is obtained by constraining parameters of the full model.
The reduced and full models use the same response observations.
The two models use compatible likelihood or loss formulations for the comparison.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The condition that regression errors follow a normal distribution conditional on predictors, used for exact small-sample t and F inference in classical models.
major_error_concepts: Claiming non-normal raw responses invalidate OLS regardless of conditional errors and inferential target.
cards.prompt: Define normal regression error assumption. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The condition that regression errors follow a normal distribution conditional on predictors, used for exact small-sample t and F inference in classical models.

cards.definition: **Definition.** For probability p, the ratio p/(1-p) of event probability to non-event probability.
major_error_concepts: Treating odds 3 as probability 3 or as a three-percentage-point increase.
cards.prompt: Define odds. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: For probability p, the ratio p/(1-p) of event probability to non-event probability.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Bias in a coefficient estimator caused when an omitted determinant of the response is associated with an included predictor under the target model.
major_error_concepts: Calling every omitted predictor a source of coefficient bias regardless of its relation to included predictors and the response.
cards.prompt: Define omitted-variable bias. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Bias in a coefficient estimator caused when an omitted determinant of the response is associated with an included predictor under the target model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The coefficient-estimation rule that minimizes the sum of squared residuals over the declared design matrix.
major_error_concepts: Defining OLS as minimizing absolute errors or assuming the minimizer is unique without a rank condition.
cards.prompt: Define ordinary least squares. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The coefficient-estimation rule that minimizes the sum of squared residuals over the declared design matrix.

cards.definition: For nested linear models fitted to the same n responses, let restricted and full design ranks be p_R<p_F<n and residual sums be RSS_R and RSS_F. The partial F statistic is [(RSS_R-RSS_F)/(p_F-p_R)]/[RSS_F/(n-p_F)]. Under the restricted mean model and independent normal errors of common positive variance conditional on the design, it has F_(p_F-p_R,n-p_F) law. It is not an exact heteroskedastic or nonnested-model test.
major_error_concepts: For any two models on different response samples, (RSS_R-RSS_F)/RSS_F is exactly F with n,n degrees of freedom.
cards.prompt: State the partial F statistic and exact null law for nested linear regression models.
required_concepts: Compare nested models on the same response data and use their design ranks.
Divide the RSS reduction by p_F-p_R and full residual mean square by n-p_F.
State the exact null F law and independent homoskedastic normal-error assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A fitting objective combining data-fit loss or negative log-likelihood with a coefficient penalty controlled by a tuning parameter.
major_error_concepts: Treating the penalty as additional observed data or claiming it leaves the original estimand and inference unchanged automatically.
cards.prompt: Define penalized regression objective. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A fitting objective combining data-fit loss or negative log-likelihood with a coefficient penalty controlled by a tuning parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The tuning parameter controlling the tradeoff between data fit and coefficient penalty in a penalized objective.
major_error_concepts: Treating lambda as a learned regression coefficient with ordinary coefficient confidence interpretation.
cards.prompt: Define regularization penalty strength. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The tuning parameter controlling the tradeoff between data fit and coefficient penalty in a penalized objective.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Conditional count variation exceeding the Poisson mean-variance relationship, often making naive Poisson standard errors too small.
major_error_concepts: Treating every poor Poisson fit as overdispersion or correcting only the mean while leaving invalid uncertainty unchanged.
cards.prompt: Define Poisson overdispersion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Conditional count variation exceeding the Poisson mean-variance relationship, often making naive Poisson standard errors too small.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A Poisson GLM, commonly with log link, for nonnegative counts or rates under an appropriate conditional mean-variance and exposure contract.
major_error_concepts: Applying Poisson regression to arbitrary positive continuous outcomes or ignoring exposure differences between counts.
cards.prompt: Define Poisson regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Poisson GLM, commonly with log link, for nonnegative counts or rates under an appropriate conditional mean-variance and exposure contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Ordinary coefficient p-values and intervals generally do not retain their nominal interpretation after data-dependent variable or penalty selection unless the selection is accounted for.
major_error_concepts: Treating the selected model as fixed in advance when computing ordinary inferential guarantees on the same data.
cards.prompt: Why can ordinary coefficient p-values and confidence intervals lose nominal validity after data-dependent model or penalty selection, and what must valid inference account for?
required_concepts: Ordinary coefficient p-values and intervals generally lose their nominal interpretation after data-dependent variable or penalty selection.
Valid post-selection interpretation requires accounting for the selection procedure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interval intended to cover one future response at specified predictors, incorporating both mean-estimation and new-observation variability.
major_error_concepts: Using only coefficient uncertainty and calling the result an individual prediction interval.
cards.prompt: Define prediction interval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interval intended to cover one future response at specified predictors, incorporating both mean-estimation and new-observation variability.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Centering and scaling predictor columns so a common coefficient penalty has a declared and comparable scale across features.
major_error_concepts: Fitting scaling parameters on validation or test data or assuming standardization makes all predictors scientifically comparable.
cards.prompt: Define predictor standardization for regularization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Centering and scaling predictor columns so a common coefficient penalty has a declared and comparable scale across features.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A measured, assigned, or constructed variable used to index conditional response behavior in a model.
major_error_concepts: Calling every predictor a causal treatment or assuming it is measured without error.
cards.prompt: Define predictor variable. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A measured, assigned, or constructed variable used to index conditional response behavior in a model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A parameter multiplying a design-matrix column, interpreted through that column's coding while holding other model columns fixed.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a multiple-regression coefficient as the unadjusted marginal association or a causal effect automatically.
cards.prompt: Define regression coefficient. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A parameter multiplying a design-matrix column, interpreted through that column's coding while holding other model columns fixed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The evidence-preserving cycle of inspecting residual and influence structure, forming a specific model-defect hypothesis, making a justified repair, and rechecking all diagnostics and estimands.
major_error_concepts: Trying transformations, exclusions, and terms until significance appears while hiding the diagnostic path and multiplicity.
cards.prompt: Define regression diagnostic-repair loop. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Inspect residual and influence structure for a reproducible diagnostic pattern.
Form a specific hypothesis about the model defect suggested by that pattern.
Make a repair justified by the defect hypothesis rather than by a desired significance result.
Refit and recheck all relevant diagnostics and estimands after the repair.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The unobserved difference between a response and its population conditional mean under the regression model.
major_error_concepts: Treating an observed residual as the true unobserved regression error.
cards.prompt: Define regression error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The unobserved difference between a response and its population conditional mean under the regression model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Using a fitted relationship at predictor combinations outside or poorly supported by the observed design region.
major_error_concepts: Treating a narrow model-based interval as evidence that an unsupported extrapolation is reliable.
cards.prompt: Define regression extrapolation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Using a fitted relationship at predictor combinations outside or poorly supported by the observed design region.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The coefficient multiplying the constant design column, interpreted as the conditional mean when all coded predictors equal zero.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting the intercept as the unconditional response mean regardless of predictor coding and model terms.
cards.prompt: Define regression intercept. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The coefficient multiplying the constant design column, interpreted as the conditional mean when all coded predictors equal zero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A quantile comparison of residuals with a reference distribution used to assess tail and shape departures relevant to error-distribution assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Using a Q-Q plot of raw responses to diagnose conditional regression errors without accounting for fitted means.
cards.prompt: What does regression residual Q-Q plot diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A quantile comparison of residuals with a reference distribution used to assess tail and shape departures relevant to error-distribution assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The observed response minus its fitted value, e_i = y_i - yhat_i, used as an estimate-related diagnostic rather than the true error.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the residual sign or equating residuals with independent model errors by definition.
cards.prompt: What does regression residual diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: The observed response minus its fitted value, e_i = y_i - yhat_i, used as an estimate-related diagnostic rather than the true error.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Penalization can add estimation bias while reducing variance or prediction instability, so lower in-sample fit need not mean worse held-out performance.
major_error_concepts: Claiming regularization uniformly improves both unbiased coefficient inference and training fit.
cards.prompt: Define regularization bias-variance tradeoff. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Penalization can add estimation bias while reducing variance or prediction instability, so lower in-sample fit need not mean worse held-out performance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The sequence of fitted coefficients across a range of penalty-strength values under fixed data and scaling.
major_error_concepts: Reading one path as repeated-sampling uncertainty or as proof of coefficient stability across new datasets.
cards.prompt: What does regularization path diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: The sequence of fitted coefficients across a range of penalty-strength values under fixed data and scaling.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Holding the design fixed, generating pseudo-responses by adding resampled fitted residuals to fitted means, then refitting under the residual-exchangeability assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Applying the ordinary residual bootstrap under strong heteroscedasticity or clustered dependence without modification.
cards.prompt: Define residual bootstrap for regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Hold the regression design matrix fixed.
Resample fitted residuals and add them to the fitted means to form pseudo-responses.
Refit the regression model to each pseudo-response sample.
The ordinary residual bootstrap relies on the residual-exchangeability assumptions, which exclude unhandled strong heteroscedasticity or clustered dependence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The number of response dimensions remaining after fitting the estimable design space, commonly n minus rank(X) for an ordinary linear model.
major_error_concepts: Computing residual degrees of freedom as n minus the raw column count when the design is rank deficient or constraints change estimability.
cards.prompt: Define residual degrees of freedom. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The number of response dimensions remaining after fitting the estimable design space, commonly n minus rank(X) for an ordinary linear model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The residual sum of squares divided by residual degrees of freedom, used to estimate common error variance under the classical linear model.
major_error_concepts: Dividing RSS by n without accounting for fitted design rank and calling the result the classical unbiased variance estimate.
cards.prompt: Define residual mean square. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The residual sum of squares divided by residual degrees of freedom, used to estimate common error variance under the classical linear model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The square root of residual mean square, estimating the common conditional error standard deviation under homoscedastic classical-model assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Treating residual standard error as a coefficient standard error or as an assumption-free prediction error estimate.
cards.prompt: Define residual standard error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The square root of residual mean square, estimating the common conditional error standard deviation under homoscedastic classical-model assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The sum of squared fitted residuals, measuring in-sample discrepancy on the response scale squared.
major_error_concepts: Summing residuals before squaring or treating RSS as directly comparable across differently scaled responses.
cards.prompt: Define residual sum of squares. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The sum of squared fitted residuals, measuring in-sample discrepancy on the response scale squared.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A plot of fitted residuals against fitted values used to reveal conditional-mean curvature, unequal variance, groups, or other unmodeled structure.
major_error_concepts: Treating a random-looking residual plot as proof that all sampling, independence, and measurement assumptions hold.
cards.prompt: What does residual-versus-fitted plot diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A plot of fitted residuals against fitted values used to reveal conditional-mean curvature, unequal variance, groups, or other unmodeled structure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The outcome whose conditional distribution or mean the model is designed to explain or predict.
major_error_concepts: Calling a variable the response solely because it appears on the left side of an arbitrary formula without a declared estimand.
cards.prompt: Define Response variable. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The outcome whose conditional distribution or mean the model is designed to explain or predict.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Penalized regression using an L2 squared-coefficient penalty that shrinks coefficients and stabilizes collinear fits without generally setting them exactly to zero.
major_error_concepts: Claiming ridge performs exact variable selection or removes the need to validate penalty strength.
cards.prompt: Define ridge regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Ridge regression uses an L2 squared-coefficient penalty to shrink coefficients.
The penalty stabilizes collinear fits without generally setting coefficients exactly to zero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A covariance-estimation form combining model sensitivity and empirical score variability to provide uncertainty robust to specified variance misspecification.
major_error_concepts: Treating any sandwich estimate as robust to arbitrary sampling bias, dependence, model selection, or few-cluster failure.
cards.prompt: Define sandwich covariance estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A covariance-estimation form combining model sensitivity and empirical score variability to provide uncertainty robust to specified variance misspecification.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A statistical model whose conditional mean is linear in unknown coefficients, commonly E[Y|X]=X beta, together with an error and sampling contract.
major_error_concepts: Defining linear regression only as a straight line in one raw predictor or omitting the error model.
cards.prompt: Define statistical linear model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A statistical model whose conditional mean is linear in unknown coefficients, commonly E[Y|X]=X beta, together with an error and sampling contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A declared family of probability distributions or conditional relationships used to represent how observed data could be generated.
major_error_concepts: Treating fitted parameter values or software output as the statistical model while omitting the family and assumptions.
cards.prompt: Define statistical model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A declared family of probability distributions or conditional relationships used to represent how observed data could be generated.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A residual scaled by an estimate of its standard deviation that accounts for residual variance and leverage.
major_error_concepts: Dividing every residual by one response standard deviation and claiming leverage-adjusted studentization.
cards.prompt: What does studentized residual diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A residual scaled by an estimate of its standard deviation that accounts for residual variance and leverage.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Testing whether a treatment contrast differs across a predeclared subgroup by estimating the treatment-by-subgroup interaction rather than separate within-group significance labels.
major_error_concepts: Inferring subgroup heterogeneity from one significant and one non-significant subgroup result without testing their difference.
cards.prompt: Define subgroup interaction analysis. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Subgroup interaction analysis tests whether a treatment contrast differs across a predeclared subgroup.
It estimates the treatment-by-subgroup interaction rather than comparing separate within-group significance labels.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A coded design column marking assigned condition membership so its coefficient or contrast represents a declared between-condition comparison under the model.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting any binary predictor coefficient as a randomized treatment effect without an assignment and analysis contract.
cards.prompt: Define treatment indicator in regression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A coded design column marking assigned condition membership so its coefficient or contrast represents a declared between-condition comparison under the model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** For a predictor column, the factor 1/(1-R_j^2) by which collinearity with other columns inflates its coefficient variance under the classical linear model.
major_error_concepts: Treating VIF as a measure of predictor importance, causal confounding, or response-model fit.
cards.prompt: What does variance inflation factor diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: For a predictor column, the factor 1/(1-R_j^2) by which collinearity with other columns inflates its coefficient variance under the classical linear model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The assumption E[epsilon|X]=0, which makes the specified conditional mean correct and supports unbiased OLS coefficient estimation under the design conditions.
major_error_concepts: Replacing zero conditional mean with the weaker sample fact that intercept-model residuals sum to zero.
cards.prompt: Define zero conditional mean error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The assumption E[epsilon|X]=0, which makes the specified conditional mean correct and supports unbiased OLS coefficient estimation under the design conditions.
